model: WTW9500E (Maytag MVWB955F in the same manual)
notes: Whirlpool's 6.2 cu ft direct-drive top loader (WTW9500E*, all colours) and its Maytag counterpart (MVWB955F*), as covered by Whirlpool's 2016 service manual. The relay expansion board, bulk dispense pump, recirculation pump and heater are on some models only; the Oxi valve is not on all models.

gaps: Years: 2015 is the year of introduction the model code key gives for the E in WTW9500E (p. 1-6); the Maytag code MVWB955F gives 2016 (F). The manual is copyright 2016.
The model code key lists B955 as 5.3 cu ft but the cover and specifications say 6.2 cu ft; no capacity is taken from the key.
The rotor magnet material is not stated; no part numbers, chip markings or pump, heater and motor wattages are printed, so none are claimed.
The text layer prints the ohm sign as W on some pages; the resistance pages (3-9, 3-11, 3-13, 3-14, 3-15, 3-18) were read from page images.
method: Whirlpool & Maytag Direct Drive Top Load Washer service manual W10864849 (Whirlpool Corporation, copyright 2016; cover names WTW9500E* and MVWB955F*), read from an Amazon S3 copy; title, part number and copyright confirmed on the cover and forward.
The maytag.com copy of the same file did not open (fetch failed, then timed out), so the S3 copy was used.
Pages read: 1-3 to 1-7, 2-5, 2-10, 2-14, 3-6, 3-7, 3-9, 3-11, 3-13, 3-14, 3-15 and 3-18; the resistance pages were rendered and read as images.
No bot check, login or paywall met. Sears PartsDirect and PartSelect were not used.

comps.spec: Direct-drive three-phase brushless permanent-magnet (BPM) motor with its stator and rotor on the drive assembly and no transmission (p. 1-3). Spin up to 1100 rpm (p. 1-7). Winding check: 8-10 ohm at drive motor connector pins 2-3 and 3-4 (p. 3-9).
Motor stator, taken off after the motor bolt, the motor cover and the shifter coil are removed (Test 3b, p. 3-9).
Rotor of the permanent-magnet motor, joined to the internal drive shaft (p. 1-3, Figure 5 on p. 1-4).
Drain pump: 18-24 ohm across its two terminals (Test 7, p. 3-13).
Recirculation pump, on some models: 26-32 ohm across its two terminals (Test 7, p. 3-13).
Bulk dispense (detergent) pump, on some models: 1485-1815 ohm at its connector (Test 12, p. 3-18).
Water valve assembly with coils for fabric softener, Oxi (not on all models), hot, cold, detergent and fresh fill; each coil reads 790-840 ohm (Test 2, p. 3-6).
Shifter (clutch) coil: an electromagnet that pulls the clutch into the rotor so the basket spins with the impeller (p. 1-4).
Spring that returns the clutch to its home position when the shifter coil is off (p. 1-4).
Lid lock motor, 12 VDC (lid lock schematic, p. 3-14): 35 ohm winding (plus or minus 5 ohm) at connector J6 pins 2 and 3 (Test 8). The lock also holds lock, home and lid switches.
Three lid lock switches (lock, home and lid), each reading 0 ohm or open circuit depending on the lock and lid state (Test 8, p. 3-14).
Water heater element, on some models, wired between the L1 and N heater relays of the main control (strip circuit, p. 3-15). An infinite resistance reading means replace it (Test 9).
Temperature thermistor on main control connector J2 pins 1-2: 10 kohm at 25 C (77 F); the table runs from 32.3 kohm at 0 C to 2.1 kohm at 65 C (Test 5, p. 3-11).
Water level pressure transducer on the main control, fed by a pressure hose from the tub (p. 2-10); the service diagnostics verification cycle has a step that validates the pressure sensor (p. 2-5).

Main control (ACU) board. Its fault list includes motor drive module over-temperature, over-current and over-voltage codes F7E2 to F7E4 (p. 2-10), and the verification cycle checks an IPM thermistor (p. 2-5).
Relay expansion (Rex) board, on some models, with connectors J1 (AC in), J2 (bulk dispense pump) and J3 (to the main control) (Test 12, p. 3-18).
Bearings: for friction or drag on the drive, the troubleshooting guide says to check the motor and bearings (p. 2-14).
